rationale.conceptual: The method uses well-established DFT (PBEsol+mBJ) and Boltzmann transport theory; extraction of exchange constants from band edges is a straightforward analysis of computed electronic structure; no new algorithms or deep theoretical derivations are required.
rationale.execution: The workflow spans several stages: structural optimization with energy-volume fitting, spin‑polarized band structure/DOS with mBJ, and Boltzmann transport post‑processing. Setting up an all‑electron full‑potential code (Wien2k) with the appropriate input parameters (RMT*Kmax, k‑mesh, muffin‑tin radii) and correctly feeding eigenvalues to BoltzTraP2 constitutes a multi‑step pipeline with non‑trivial tooling, though still within the scope of a single computational campaign.

difficulty.reasoning: Standard DFT+transport calculation on known spinel compounds; the conceptual task is routine in computational materials science, while the execution pipeline involves multiple steps with specialized codes (Wien2k, BoltzTraP2) but is not excessively long.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT calculations on two small unit cells (14 atoms each) with an all‑electron LAPW code; CPU‑only runtime, peak memory modest (~8 GB), no large external datasets.
